title_ar: الشيخ الددو يلقي محاضرات فكرية ودعوية في تونس الشقيقة
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Delivers Lectures on Thought and Daʿwah in Sister Tunisia
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء سلسلة محاضرات خلال زيارته لدولة تونس الشقيقة، التي تستغرق ثلاثة أيام ابتداءً من السبت 25 صفر 1435هـ، الموافق 28 دجنبر 2013م، شملت الزيارة إلقاء محاضرتيْن في ملتقى الفكر الثاني المنظم من طرف جمعية الدعوة والإصلاح في منطقة "قبلي" في جنوب تونس حول الفقه الإسلامي وإشكاليات الحكم، وكان موضوعا المحاضرتيْن عن الأساليب الحديثة للحكم الديمقراطي؛ نموذج في الاتفاق والاختلاف مع الشورى وكذلك موضوع الولاء والبراء..

وتشمل أيضا هذه الزيارة إلقاء محاضرات في مدينتيْ قابس وجربه في أقصى الجنوب التونسي، بالإضافة إلى بعض الأنشطة الثقافية التي سيقوم بها في العاصمة التونسية قبل انتهاء الزيارة.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a series of lectures during his visit to the sister state of Tunisia — a visit lasting three days, beginning on Saturday 25 Safar 1435 AH, corresponding to 28 December 2013. The visit included the delivery of two lectures at the Second Forum on Thought, organised by the Association for Daʿwah and Reform in the "Qibli" (Kebili) region in southern Tunisia, on Islamic jurisprudence and the problems of governance. The subjects of the two lectures were the modern methods of democratic rule — a case study in where they agree with, and where they differ from, consultation (shūrā) — and likewise the subject of loyalty and disavowal (al-walāʾ wa-l-barāʾ)…

This visit also includes the delivery of lectures in the cities of Gabès and Djerba in the far south of Tunisia, in addition to some cultural activities that he will undertake in the Tunisian capital before the visit ends.

flags.context: the announced subject of the second lecture in Tunisia
options: solidarity [with the believers] and repudiation [of unbelief]
flags.note: EDITORIAL. Not in the glossary; a candidate for addition. The pairing carries very different weight in different hands: in classical Maliki and Ashʿari usage it concerns the direction of a believer's love and allegiance, while in some modern movements it has been made a basis for takfīr and for political dissociation, and the phrase is treated as a marker of extremism by some Western commentators and agencies. This record is a three-line announcement of a lecture TITLE; the lecture itself is not in the corpus, so nothing here establishes which sense the Sheikh gave it. The English must not be captioned as stating his position. Flagged, not resolved.

flags.arabic: الأساليب الحديثة للحكم الديمقراطي؛ نموذج في الاتفاق والاختلاف مع الشورى
flags.context: the announced subject of the first lecture
options: a case study in where they agree with, and where they differ from, consultation (shūrā)
a model of agreement and disagreement with shūrā
a comparison of modern democratic governance with shūrā
flags.note: نموذج في الاتفاق والاختلاف is compressed to the point of ambiguity even in Arabic: it may mean a worked example, a model, or a type-case. The English is kept neutral so that it does not imply the Sheikh either endorsed or rejected democratic government. The lecture is not in this record.

flags.context: the place of the Second Forum on Thought
flags.note: A Tunisian governorate in the south, usually written Kébili or Kebili in English. The Arabic name is kept and the usual English spelling supplied in brackets so the place can be identified.

translator_notes: An announcement only. The record is 635 characters and contains no content from any of the lectures it names: the site is reporting a trip, not publishing a text. It must not be displayed as a lecture.
دجنبر is the Maghrebi form of 'December'.
قابس وجربه are Gabès and Djerba, given in their standard English spellings per style guide section 2.
